title: spec review: Active path 1: context_router active sends the routed evidence packet to execute and review workers (byte change gated by mode), with recovery logging
spec:
Today (T-0800) context_router mode "active" is treated as shadow with a one-time warning in spawn._shadow_route / the packet builders. Build the real active branch. Facts: spawn._packet_body assembles sections (objective, acceptance, base, write_scope, read_scope, constraints, relevant_tests, symbols, gotchas, decisions, verify, evidence, dependencies) and caps at 4800 chars; the shadow path builds Evidence candidates and context_router.route()/render() produce a routed "## evidence (routed v1)" block plus per-item levels; review_packet does the same for the diff. The eval suite (orchestrator context-eval, T-0841) checks seven fixture categories.
Do:
1. Active for execute: when promotion.mode("context_router") == "active", the sections symbols, gotchas, decisions, evidence and read_scope are REPLACED by the routed rendering of their candidates (HIDE items omitted, SHORT one-liners, LONG summaries, FULL verbatim), while objective, acceptance, base, write_scope, constraints, relevant_tests, verify and dependencies stay exactly as today (hard constraints: task contract and failing output are never routed away). The 4800-char cap still applies after routing; the packet header records "routed v1 active".
2. Active for review and security_review: the diff stays FULL for in-scope files; prior review findings and previous results follow the routed levels; the security section is never routed away.
3. Recovery logging (P21 context_recovery_rate): when a worker running under an active packet later reads a file whose evidence was HIDE or SHORT (jev_gate read_economy classification sees the Read), record a decision_log row kind "evidence_reuse" with reason "recovery_read" and the evidence id; context_scorecard exposes recovery_rate = recovery reads / hidden items per role; `scorecard --economy` shows it.
4. Safety: active is refused (falls back to shadow with a notify line) when the last .orchestrator/context_eval.json is missing, older than 7 days, or suite_passed is false. Document this in docs/context-economy/05-context-router.md (Active section) with the revert path (mode back to shadow).
Tests (unittest): tests/test_spawn.py::test_execute_packet_active_replaces_routed_sections_only (objective/acceptance/write_scope identical to shadow; symbols/gotchas replaced by the routed block; HIDE items absent), ::test_review_packet_active_keeps_diff_and_security_section, ::test_active_refused_without_passing_context_eval (mode active + no context_eval.json → packet equals shadow packet and a notify line mentions the refusal); tests/test_context_scorecard.py::test_recovery_rate_from_evidence_reuse_rows. context-eval must still pass in both modes (add an "active" column to its table: routed packet text length).
Do not ask questions; decide and note decisions in the result. Never quote double-brace placeholder tokens literally.
acceptance: `uv run orchestrator context-eval` exits 0 with the active column; docs/context-economy/05-context-router.md has an Active section; .claude/hooks/tests-green.sh exits 0

risks.issue: The 'symbols' section (spawn.py:398-412, list built at 298-317) has no dedicated evidence type in _packet_body's candidate list — only full-file source_chunk evidence exists for scope files (lines 423-426), which is always FULL for in-scope files per context_router._choice's 'in_scope_file' rule. Replacing 'symbols' (today a compact name+lineno list) with 'routed rendering of its candidates' means injecting up to 12000 chars of verbatim source per scope file into every execute packet — content never shown today — and those FULL items are hard constraints in decision_row, so the existing 4800-char trim loop (which only pops lines from sections named in `trimmable`, not FULL/hard-constraint items) may be unable to bring the packet back under cap.

read_economy.classify(call, history) is called at line 372 without evidence= or head_sha=, so the 'evidence_available' classification path (read_economy.py's _has_evidence) is currently dead code in production. Point 3 assumes jev_gate can already tell whether a Read hits HIDE/SHORT evidence, but classify() only returns a binary evidence_available/not, not a level — detecting 'HIDE or SHORT' requires new wiring (thread the task's EvidencePool + head_sha into the gate, then cross-reference the latest context_selection decision_log row's per-item levels for that task). None of this wiring is described, and no acceptance test exercises jev_gate itself — only context_scorecard's aggregation of pre-fabricated decision rows is tested, so an executor could satisfy every acceptance test while leaving point 3's actual detection unimplemented.

Point 2 gives no section name/location for where routed 'prior review findings and previous results' should render in review_packet — unlike point 1's explicit five-section list for execute. The only existing section that carries prior review content is 'fix-round context' (lines 647-661), which is conditional on fix_round_for and today shows raw comment JSON, not review_finding/previous_result evidence. The acceptance test test_review_packet_active_keeps_diff_and_security_section only checks diff+security presence, so this ambiguity has no verifiable acceptance target.

The cap-trim loop (lines 463-482) pops one trailing line at a time from a section's `lines` list, assuming independent bullet lines. Once a replaced section's lines are a routed LONG/FULL block containing a fenced code segment (context_router._text emits ```` ```\ncontent\n``` ````), popping the last line first removes the closing fence, leaving an unterminated code block in the packet body for every subsequent trim iteration.

Point 1 requires the packet header to record 'routed v1 active', but packet()'s header (lines 544-548) and packet_run_meta's parser (lines 507-517, including the legacy `pool.toml@(\S+) gotchas@(\S+)` sub-match) have a fixed shape. The spec doesn't say where the new marker is inserted, risking either breaking the legacy sources sub-match or being silently unparsed by packet_run_meta.

collect() already computes a 'context_recovery_rate' field (this file, recovery_rows filter) keyed on decision_log kind 'read_economy' — a kind jev_gate never actually writes (it writes kind='action_gate' at jev_gate.py:392). The new spec adds a second, differently-named recovery signal (kind 'evidence_reuse') consumed by context_scorecard. Two divergently-named, non-overlapping 'recovery rate' computations will coexist without reconciliation, which is confusing for anyone reading scorecard output.

suggested_spec_changes: For execute: name the exact evidence source_type each replaced section draws from (symbols vs read_scope both currently map to source_chunk candidates with no disambiguation), and either cap FULL in-scope-source rendering outside the 4800 budget or drop 'symbols' from the replaced-section list.
For review/security_review: name the exact section (new or existing) that receives the routed findings/results block, and add an acceptance assertion that routed content actually appears there.

Specify the jev_gate wiring (EvidencePool + head_sha threaded into read_economy.classify, plus a level lookup against the task's context_selection decision row) needed before claiming recovery detection 'sees the Read', and add an acceptance test that exercises jev_gate's detection directly, not only context_scorecard's aggregation of synthetic rows.
Specify exactly where 'routed v1 active' is inserted in the packet header so packet_run_meta's existing sources-regex still parses correctly.
Have the cap-trim loop treat a routed section's rendering as an atomic block (trim by removing lowest-priority whole items, not trailing lines) so fenced code segments can't be left unterminated.
